summary: Published node2's TCP/8080 app to node3 through node1 (VyOS router) using Ansible run from node4, the pre-provisioned control node. Built a private point-to-point network (10.10.20.0/24) between node1 eth1 and node2 enp8s0, deployed a systemd-managed demo app on node2 bound only to its private IP, and configured VyOS on node1 with a destination-NAT rule (eth0:8080 -> 10.10.20.2:8080) plus a default-drop forward filter that permits only established/related traffic and the specific tcp/8080 flow to 10.10.20.2, so nothing else in the private network is exposed to node3. Fixed an asymmetric-routing issue (node2 is dual-homed onto the same subnet as node3) via a source-based policy route on node2, and bound firewalld's zone to the NetworkManager connection profile so the private IP/route/zone all survive reboots. Verified with curl from node3 (200 OK with expected content) and confirmed an unrelated port (8081) on node2 is unreachable from node3, proving only the intended port is forwarded. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id and service/functional baselines on all four nodes, restarted each one at a time (node3, node4, node2, node1) via systemctl reboot, confirmed a changed boot_id on each, and re-verified the full functional chain (and re-ran the Ansible playbook end-to-end) after every restart. Along the way discovered and fixed a persistence bug: the initial SSH key placed directly in VyOS's authorized_keys file did not survive reboot (VyOS regenerates that file from its own config), so it was moved into VyOS's `system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config, making Ansible's access to node1 durable across restarts.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: topology, OS (VyOS/RHEL9/RHEL9/Ubuntu), interfaces, and identified node4 as the control node with ansible-core pre-installed
Set up passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2 and node3 (root)
Diagnosed and worked around VyOS 'configure' session requiring root privilege (sudo) over SSH to avoid 'without config session' errors
Discovered current VyOS release's firewall 'state' node syntax changed (no trailing 'enable') vs older documented syntax
Wrote inventory.ini and playbook.yml on node4 under /root/ansible-portforward/

Play 1 (node2): nmcli-configured static private IP 10.10.20.2/24 on enp8s0, firewalld zone 'privatelan' scoped to that interface with only 8080/tcp open, source-based policy route for return-path symmetry, and a systemd unit serving the demo app bound to the private IP

Play 2 (node1/VyOS via raw+become sudo): set eth1 10.10.20.1/24, NAT destination rule 10 (eth0:8080 -> 10.10.20.2:8080), forward filter default-action drop + established/related + specific rule for 10.10.20.2:8080 only, committed and saved
Play 3 (node3): verified curl to node1 published port returns the app content; verified direct access to the private IP times out

Iteratively debugged and fixed: firewalld zone creation/reload ordering, VyOS raw command quirks (set -e vs commit rc=1 on no-op), asymmetric routing on node2, and firewalld zone not surviving NetworkManager connection cycling
Manually confirmed only port 8080 is forwarded (test listener on 8081 unreachable from node3)
Ran mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all 4 nodes sequentially, capturing boot_id before/after and re-verifying functional recovery (and Ansible re-run) after each
Fixed VyOS SSH-key persistence by moving it into system login config instead of raw authorized_keys file

evidence.requirement: App published from node2 reachable by node3 through node1 on port 8080
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to node1's eth0 IP (10.100.5.10:8080) returns HTTP 200 with node2's content, both manually and via the Ansible playbook's verification play

evidence.requirement: Rest of the private network is NOT opened to node3
evidence.summary: Ansible verification task shows a direct attempt from node3 to the private IP (10.10.20.2:8080) fails (rc=28 timeout / 000); a second test listener on port 8081 on node2 is unreachable from node3 via node1 (rc=7, connection refused), proving only the specific forwarded port is exposed

evidence.requirement: Implementation performed via Ansible from the correct control node
